notes:
Key negotiation points + call notes:
- Customer explicit ask: 'We need predictable throughput, not just best-effort — business-critical routing depends on it.'
- Minimum guaranteed throughput: Oxbridge asking for cluster-level commit that maps to ~80k sustained tokens/sec during peak windows (8–18 local time). They view this as a gating item for procurement.
- Concurrency caps: want a hard concurrency guarantee for their transactional sessions (target 250 concurrent sessions sustained) and defined behavior when cap is hit (queue + degrade).
- Burst policy: asks for short bursts to 600 concurrent sessions for 5–10 minutes; willing to pay higher unit price for burst capacity. Wants explicit billing formula for burst usage and clear demarcation between committed and burst units.
- Fallbacks: prefer automatic routing to quantized variant (lower cost, lower quality) rather than dropping requests. Also want cache-first routing for repeated prefixes.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95 targets discussed. Customer insists on token-level latency breakouts in contract and credits if SLO missed.
- Redwood proposals so far: three SLA tiers (Gold/Silver/Bronze) mapped to different committed tokens/sec and concurrency. Engineering suggested a canary window (2 weeks) followed by committed start date.
- POC plan: synthetic replay of 72 hours of historical traffic (anonymized CSV provided) to validate sustained tokens/sec and p95 percentiles. SE will instrument per-token timing, KV cache hit rate, and batching efficiency.
- Commercials: Redwood priced a committed token bucket + overage for bursts, and also offered an alternative model with reserved GPU counts (8 x A100 equiv) + support credits. Finance to model both.
- Security: infosec requires SOC2 + KMS demo; added request for audit log extract format and retention policy examples.
- Quote blockers: internal legal wants explicit MTTR definition, credit math, and clear termination clauses tied to SLA failures. Budget owner (VP Ops) needs ARR impact model before sign-off.
- Direct quote from Head of Platform: 'If you can guarantee this throughput and give us transparent billing during spikes, we can move to a year commit.'
- Next immediate actions: Redwood to send draft SLA with numeric min tokens/sec and concurrency caps (Jordan + Priya to own), engineering to prepare synthetic POC harness (run week of 2026-03-01), legal to be looped after draft (Ethan to coordinate).
